ExA-SPIM 2024 · author estimate

Expansion microscopy

2024 · year as printed in Table A1

≈100 billion voxels/$

≈$1×10⁻¹¹ per voxel

Illustrative human-brain acquisition cost: $18.75B per human brain

Illustrative conversion: 1.875×10²¹ voxels (~1.9 sextillion), at 4×4×40 nm across 1,200,000 mm³, ÷ source-estimated voxels per dollar. Image acquisition only; excludes preparation, reconstruction, proofreading and storage. Optical and EM scopes and resolutions differ; this is not a matched whole-brain project budget.

Acquisition-efficiency estimate: Compiling molecular ultrastructure into neural dynamics — arXiv:2603.25713v1, Table A1 (p. 18) ↗

ExA-SPIM method: Glaser et al. (2025) · Expansion-assisted selective plane illumination microscopy for nanoscale imaging of centimeter-scale tissues ↗

Table A1 row 2: ExA-SPIM; Approx. Voxels/$ = 100,000,000,000. Rough order-of-magnitude author estimate. Method reference: Glaser et al. (2025), Expansion-assisted selective plane illumination microscopy for nanoscale imaging of centimeter-scale tissues, eLife 12, RP91979. The specific throughput/cost assumptions behind this efficiency estimate remain unverified. The plotted year is 2024 as printed in Table A1; the method paper was published in 2025.
